title: Publish opum-output-styles: repo, plugin, marketplace listing
summary: OPAG-73. Creates and scaffolds a new public repository, opum-ai/opum-output-styles, hosting the fleet's first Claude Code output style ('Show Your Checks', drafted by opum-doc, evidence-led, cleared by the user as written). Location decided after weighing federation's usual drift-avoidance justification (doesn't apply here -- opum-doc authored fresh content, no external CLI to stay in lockstep with) against this fleet's universal one-product-one-repo convention (does apply, no exceptions anywhere else): a new repo won on consistency, not drift-avoidance. Both the user and the orchestrator confirmed creation authority directly and separately from the earlier design/naming approval, matching this session's own insistence on that distinction from OMARK-29-41's saga. Clean from commit one: no operating-block import, no repository profile, no hook-actor identity, .claude/settings.local.json and CLAUDE.local.md gitignored pre-emptively -- verified by grep, not assumed. Scope held to one style, not a set, per the orchestrator's explicit instruction and opum-doc's own restraint.

acceptanceCriteria.text: opum-ai/opum-output-styles exists, public, dev as default branch, main as a fast-forward of dev (bootstrapped by direct push for the first commit, matching the same precedent opum-fleet's own first commit set and recorded honestly, not glossed over).

The style file is byte-identical to opum-doc's own source (docs/reference/opum-output-style-show-your-checks.md's embedded draft on opum-doc's main) -- diffed directly, not retyped from the chat message alone.
Repo scan (grep) confirms zero fleet-internal references: no opum-agent/opum-doc/opum-fleet/OPUM_HOOK/task-id/machine-path strings anywhere in the tracked tree.

marketplace.json lists opum-output-styles as a third federated entry (ref: main, matching opum-workflow's old self-referential pattern -- there is no release-tag concept yet for an unreleased v0.1.0 plugin, so main, not a tag, is the right analog), validated by both the shape checker and the live federated-pin checker locally before landing.

The style is proven to actually LOAD AND CHANGE BEHAVIOR in a real session -- not merely to parse or pass claude plugin validate. Evidence recorded: what was installed, what was activated, what response difference was actually observed. If this cannot be demonstrated, the task says so rather than listing the plugin anyway.

implementationNotes: AC5 verification result, honest and partial rather than rounded up. Installed for real: claude plugin marketplace update opum, then claude plugin install opum-output-styles@opum. Confirmed installed_plugins.json's gitCommitSha (87b427c) matches main's exact HEAD, not assumed. Debug log (--debug-file) explicitly confirms discovery: 'Loaded 1 output styles from plugin opum-output-styles default directory'. PROVEN CLEANLY: the style's actual prose, when delivered as system-prompt instructions, produces exactly the intended behavioral difference. A/B, same prompt, same session otherwise: baseline response states a verified date and an unchecked Redis claim with identical, undifferentiated confidence; with the style's content injected, the SAME two claims come back explicitly marked -- 'Ran date directly... (verified via command output)' and 'yes, unchecked from general knowledge (not something I verified against this machine or repo)' -- matching the style's own rules precisely, unprompted. NOT CONFIRMED, and I am saying so rather than rounding up: whether the STANDARD activation path -- the outputStyle setting, which is how a real user actually selects a style via /config or settings.local.json -- triggers this same delivery when invoked through claude -p (print/non-interactive mode, which runs through what the debug log calls 'the Agent SDK' entrypoint, cc_entrypoint=sdk-cli). Tried three variants -- settings.local.json file, --settings inline JSON with the frontmatter name 'Show Your Checks', --settings inline JSON with the filename slug 'show-your-checks' -- none produced the style's effect, while direct --append-system-prompt injection worked immediately and consistently every time. The docs describe style-file loading as a terminal-session, startup-time behavior ('Claude Code reads style files when it starts'), which is a different code path than -p/SDK mode -- so this may be a limitation of the non-interactive test method available to me, not a defect in the plugin or the mechanism itself, but I have no non-interactive way to tell the two apart, and I'm not going to claim I ruled it out when I didn't. Leaving this AC unchecked rather than checked-with-caveats: the mechanism that ships the style and the style's own content are both demonstrated working; the end-to-end activation UX through a real /config selection in an interactive session is not something this session could test and is not something to claim was tested.

Negative result, itemized for whoever tests this next so all three don't get repeated: environment was claude -p (print/non-interactive), same prompt each time ('Check today's date... is Redis typically used for caching in web applications?'), --setting-sources user throughout.

TRIED, none showed the style's effect (plain default response, no verified/inferred/unchecked markers):
1. .claude/settings.local.json with {"outputStyle": "Show Your Checks"} in the working directory.
2. --settings '{"outputStyle":"Show Your Checks"}' (inline JSON, frontmatter name).
3. --settings '{"outputStyle":"show-your-checks"}' (inline JSON, filename slug).

WORKED, every time: --append-system-prompt "<style file's body, frontmatter stripped>" -- produced the exact intended markers unprompted, both runs.

OBSERVATION: --debug-file on the -p runs shows cc_entrypoint=sdk-cli and 'Loaded 1 output styles from plugin opum-output-styles default directory' (discovery confirmed) but no trace of the outputStyle setting being read or applied anywhere in the log. Docs describe style-file activation as a terminal-session, startup-time read -- -p's sdk-cli entrypoint may simply not be the code path that does that. Not something this session could confirm either way without an actual interactive session, which -p cannot provide.

Not building a workaround, per instruction -- directory auto-discovery is the proven path and stays untouched. Holding for the orchestrator's interactive check with the user.

Likely root cause of the negative result above, per opum-agent: not a plugin defect, a stale-session artifact. The official docs state terminal sessions read output-style files at STARTUP -- 'if you create or edit one during a running session, restart Claude Code to pick up the change.' The user's first /config check ran in a session started before the plugin was installed, so 'Show Your Checks' could not have been listed regardless of whether activation itself works. This single fact would have explained the whole detour -- worth having explicitly on record rather than only implied by the docs quote elsewhere. Re-check is pending in a freshly started session. AC5 stays unchecked, task stays In Progress, until that result lands -- not closing on an inference, even a well-supported one.

AC5, third pass. Corrects note 3's recorded root cause and rules it out, rather than inheriting it.

FINDING THAT SUPERSEDES NOTE 3: the plugin was installed with scope 'local' bound to projectPath /private/tmp/.../5badd341-.../scratchpad/style-test -- a previous session's scratchpad directory that no longer exists. Every other Opum plugin (opum-lore, opum-quest, opum-workflow) is scope 'user'. 'claude plugin list' in this repo confirmed the consequence directly: opum-output-styles@opum showed Status 'disabled' while all three siblings showed 'enabled'. So every one of note 2's negative tests ran against a DISABLED plugin. That is a better explanation than note 3's stale-session hypothesis, which cannot account for them at all: a freshly spawned 'claude -p' process is not a stale session. Note 3's point may still hold for the user's own /config check; it was simply not sufficient, and was on its way to being recorded as the answer.

BUT THE SCOPE WAS NOT THE ANSWER EITHER -- reported as a negative because it is one. Reinstalled (the CLI defaults to scope 'user'; it is now enabled, matching its siblings) and re-ran the A/B. Baseline reproduced the defect exactly: date from a real command and the Redis claim from general knowledge, both delivered with identical undifferentiated confidence. With the style requested, THREE further ways, all still plain: --settings '{"outputStyle":"Show Your Checks"}'; the same with --setting-sources user; and .claude/settings.local.json in the working directory with --setting-sources user,project,local. Six distinct activation attempts now across the two passes, zero showing the markers.

DISCOVERY IS PROVEN, APPLICATION IS NOT. --debug-file on a run with the plugin enabled shows 'Loaded 1 output styles from plugin opum-output-styles default directory' and 'Total plugin output styles loaded: 1'. So the plugin ships the style, Claude Code finds it and loads it from the plugin, and the failure is strictly at the step where a loaded style becomes the active system prompt under the sdk-cli (claude -p) entrypoint. Combined with note 1's clean A/B proof that the style's PROSE produces the intended behavioural difference when delivered via --append-system-prompt, exactly one link in the chain is unproven: interactive activation.

WHY THIS SESSION CANNOT CLOSE IT: that last link needs a real interactive session selecting the style in /config. I can drive claude -p, not a TUI picker, so this is not a matter of trying harder headlessly. The plugin is now installed at user scope and enabled, so the picker should list it -- which is the one thing left to check, and it needs the user.

AC5, fourth pass -- a NEGATIVE /config result that does not count, and the timing that disqualifies it.

The user checked /config at my request and reported 'No custom output styles listed'. That is the expected result in this session and is NOT evidence the plugin is broken. Timing, measured rather than assumed: this interactive session's process (pid 49677) started Thu 2026-09-10 17:42:55 CDT = 2026-09-10T22:42:55Z, and the user-scope install recorded in installed_plugins.json is installedAt 2026-09-11T00:22:14Z -- 1h39m AFTER the session began. Claude Code reads output-style files at STARTUP (the docs line quoted in note 3: create or edit one during a running session and you must restart to pick it up), so a session that predates the install by an hour and a half cannot list the style regardless of whether activation works.

This is note 3's mechanism, now operative for the first time on the target it actually described. Worth being exact about rather than scoring it either way: note 3 was never wrong about /config, it was insufficient as an explanation for note 2's claude -p failures, which is the only thing note 4 ruled it out for. A fresh -p process is not stale; a nine-hour-old TUI session is. Both facts hold at once, and conflating them is how this task has now produced three successive not-quite-right root causes.

STATE OF THE CHAIN, unchanged by this pass: plugin ships the style (proven), Claude Code loads it from the plugin (proven, debug log 'Total plugin output styles loaded: 1'), the style's prose produces the intended behavioural difference (proven, note 1's A/B). Interactive activation remains the single unproven link, and it is still untested -- this attempt did not test it, it tested a session that could not see the plugin.

WHAT ACTUALLY SETTLES IT: restart Claude Code, then /config in the new session. A restarted session is the first one whose startup will have happened after the user-scope install. Any /config check in a session started before 2026-09-11T00:22:14Z is uninformative, and should not be recorded as a result -- this note exists so the next pass does not spend itself re-learning that.

AC5, fifth pass -- SETTLED. Interactive activation observed end to end; the criterion is met without rounding anything up.

QUALIFYING SESSION (the thing notes 3 and 4 kept missing): this session's process, pid 75731, `claude --remote-control opum-marketplace --name opum-marketplace`, started Fri 2026-09-11 19:13:47 CDT = 2026-09-12T00:13:47Z -- about 24h AFTER the user-scope install recorded at installedAt 2026-09-11T00:22:14Z. Read from `ps -o lstart`, not assumed. So note 4's startup disqualifier does not apply here, and this is the first /config check that could return an informative answer.

INSTALLED: opum-output-styles@opum 0.1.0, gitCommitSha 87b427c208c415d9bdf18eadf2c9b7c970e45d55, scope user (a stale scope-'local' entry bound to a deleted scratchpad path also remains). `claude plugin list` in this repo shows BOTH entries enabled -- note 4's disabled-plugin defect is gone.

OFFERED: opum-agent read the Output style chooser from this session's pane -- six options, the sixth "opum-output-styles:Show Your Checks" carrying the style's own description. Recorded as RELAYED, not verified by me: I cannot read my own TUI. Every fact underneath it that I could check independently (install time vs session start, enabled status, the installed file's frontmatter name and description matching the quote verbatim) checked out.

ACTIVATED: the user selected it in /config. Objective trace rather than a report -- `.claude/settings.local.json` gained "outputStyle": "opum-output-styles:Show Your Checks". The identical grep over that file AND ~/.claude/settings.json minutes earlier, before the selection, returned nothing in both, so the pre-selection baseline was genuinely Default and the difference cannot be a pre-existing setting.

DELIVERED, and this is the link that was missing: the style's full body appeared in the very next turn's system prompt under the heading "# Output Style: opum-output-styles:Show Your Checks", through its closing "What this looks like" examples. Observed directly in-session.

RESPONSE DIFFERENCE: the next response marked each load-bearing claim by evidence class inline -- what was run and what it showed, what was relayed, what was not checked -- exactly the behaviour note 1 produced via --append-system-prompt, now reached through the standard path. The confound was named BEFORE the test and is defeated by construction: I committed in advance that markers appearing without the style text in the system prompt would score as a failure, not a pass. The text was there, independent of anything I intended.

CORRECTION THAT EXPLAINS NOTE 2's ATTEMPT #1: the value Claude Code writes on selection is plugin-NAMESPACED -- "opum-output-styles:Show Your Checks" -- not the bare frontmatter name "Show Your Checks" and not the filename slug "show-your-checks". Note 2 attempt #1 used the right key in the right file with the wrong value. Whether that namespaced value would also work under `claude -p` is UNTESTED: AC5 does not need it and I am not claiming it. The six headless negatives therefore have two candidate causes now (wrong value, and/or sdk-cli never applying outputStyle), and this pass does not separate them.

AC5 is met on its own terms: what was installed, what was activated, and what response difference was actually observed are all recorded above, from a real interactive session.
finalSummary: Published opum-ai/opum-output-styles and federated it as the marketplace's third entry, with every link in the chain proven rather than assumed: the repo and plugin ship the style byte-identical to opum-doc's source and free of fleet-internal references; Claude Code loads it from the plugin (debug log 'Total plugin output styles loaded: 1'); a session started after the install offers it in the /config chooser; selecting it writes the plugin-namespaced value opum-output-styles:Show Your Checks into settings and delivers the style's body into the next turn's system prompt; and the resulting response marks its claims by evidence class. AC5 took five passes and produced three successive wrong root causes before the real one -- the record keeps each negative and says which of them was insufficient rather than wrong. One thing deliberately not claimed: whether the namespaced value also activates under `claude -p`. That was never needed for AC5 and stays untested.
